_about: PARKED. How each fighter bends the grammar (docs/combat/moveset-generator.md section 2), as Orb confirmed it on 2026-10-05 (docs/ep/vision.md, questionnaire 17): the Protagonist is palms, blade hands and arcs; the rival is fists, plates and straight lines, with fists on his heavies and blade hands on his lights. A weight multiplies a shape's score; a tip is written limb.tip. Fighter keys are the neutral working ids.

rival._waves: Animation's manifests that hold his posed strikes; a later wave's row replaces an earlier one's for the same strike

weightsBy._why: Orb: blade hands on his lights
Orb: fists on what were his heavies, the mediums now
a show-off: fists, plates and his shoulder, on lines and from above, at the head and chest where it is seen

never.why: Orb: a closed fist on what were his heavies and his enders, the mediums now, and on the new heavies; a plate may lead
Orb's split gives him fists, plates and blade hands: no palm strike. His posed palm heel and double palm stay posed and out of his cells; a rising palm is the Protagonist's
the crescent and the hook kick are the Protagonist's

rival._tipFlags: how he shows a tip, as a pose flag for Legal's rows: his palm is drawn clawed (wave 1). He has no palm strike today; if one returns, a palm of his to the head or jaw is refused (b06)

reach._hands: fists and plates up close, beside the blade hand: his lights are blade hands, so three of his four point-blank bolts are a blade hand and one is the lit fist; his mediums are fists, so his blast is the lit fist with the plate behind it. Legal's e06 names the lit fist as his third hand (e9a57791). No open palm here: it is an energy hand of his at range, and he has no palm as a strike
reach._posed: the key sets Animation drew for his energy pieces in reach, by hand, release and place. The first rule that fits a piece is its key set; a rule with a strike id makes the piece posed, and that id is what the recipes and the director name. The ids are Animation's: the rival's flick and sweep have ids of his own (strike.bolt_flick_gut, strike.bolt_sweep_chest), since both fighters had them under one id on different places and the pieces table is one row an id. A rule may carry strikeNow, the id a pack has today, while a rename is on its way; none does now

specials._about: His three specials (docs/combat/pending/wave7-first-kit.md). Which sits on X, Y and A is Combat's guess until Game Design rules

x.what: a sudden change of level and a wide cutting blow as he arrives

entry: a dash from out of reach

y.what: both arms open through a half turn and a fan of shards leaves along the sweep

range: a tight fan that ends in the ring
place: one arm, braced off a wall

a.what: a grab at speed, a drag along the ground on the rival's back, and a throw
a.status: designed (wave 7), waits for the held state

reach: a dash, or a skid on the ground
place: a dive carrying him, then the spike

manner._about: How he throws, in words, for Animation and Legal. Not read by the generator
manner.heavy: A show-off. He lets the rival see it coming: the tell is held open to view with the chin up, the blow travels in the straightest line that drive allows, and he leaves the limb out for a beat after it lands, 12 ticks or fewer. The limb stays drawn back through the tell: never arms spread as an invitation, never a beckon, and no taunt is part of a blow (Legal's h07). Never a second motion on the same wind-up
manner.burst: A show of speed: blade hands that flick out and back with the elbow high, then a straight he leaves out for a beat
manner.reach: A show of it, in straight lines. A blade hand driven in flat with the forearm plate behind it, the light a thin edge along the plate and off the flat of the hand: a flat blade, never a pointed finger. And the lit fist, thrown as a straight punch whose shot leaves the knuckle edges. His blast is the lit fist braced against him and let go along the forearm

rival._pinned: shapes a cell takes first, before its quotas. Here: the two heavies Animation is already studying on provisional poses (data/anim/waves/rival7: su_ram, a long low lunge behind one straight fist; su_heel, a heel brought down on the chest)

burst._close: what his burst's eighth blow is, when the rules allow: a straight

rival._reaimed: rows whose place was moved after Legal screened them (Game Design's ruling on the wrench, 68b9a586): the same limb, tip, path and drive, another place. The sheet marks them for Legal
rival._tierWaves: packs whose strikes are heavies of the new tier: Animation's weight heavy there is this file's heavy, and each row is read by the heavy tier's own tips
rival._adds: Places added to a cell for the split by path (cells.json `_quotasSplit`): his locked moves leave a group under 5, and the added place is filled by that group's quota
rival._chargedHeavy: His charged heavy as Game Design names it (fighter-pipeline.md section 8: the Protagonist's a coiled palm strike, the Anti-hero's a ram behind the plate). The pool builder keeps it in the held B's pool whatever its path; not read by the generator

martial.x.name: straight fists behind the plate (the jab, the cross and the spear hand as fists), for his perfect follow-up

martial.a.clinch.name: an elbow into the same bruise
a knee to the hurt side

rival._cellQuotas: Quotas of his row, read before the cell's, so a place added in `adds` goes to the piece Game Design's section 8 and the tenth round name (docs/combat/split-and-pieces.md section 5): the Protagonist's second falling launcher (the spike) and his turning palm (a palm travels only straight or up, so it is the heel of the hand on an arc); the Anti-hero's straight fists behind the plate, the jab, the cross and the spear hand as fists (the plate never travels straight; Animation drew all three in rival9)
rival._skillAlso: Moves pinned into the skill strike's pool whatever their form, once posed: his straight fists behind the plate (the jab, the cross and the spear hand as fists) are flurry lights by the grammar, and Game Design names it his perfect follow-up (fighter-pipeline.md section 8)

specials._about: PLACEHOLDERS. His specials are not designed: these three frames are Combat's first offer, for Game Design and Orb, so that his charging row is not empty on the sheet

x.what: a turn that carries him round the rival, and an arc as he arrives

y.what: three curving shots released one after another from the ring hand, each bent a different way

a.what: an open-hand redirect that takes the rival's line past him and leaves him on the far side

manner._about: How he throws, in words, for Animation and Legal. Not read by the generator
manner.heavy: Pointed, not cruel. One line to one point: the tell is compact and close to the body, the turn does the work, the blow stops at the target and he is back in his guard at once. No flourish before it and none after
manner.burst: A run of open hands that each find a different point: the wrist, the ribs, the collar, the jaw. It ends on an arc
manner.reach: Pointed, not cruel: the heel of the palm set on one point, the chest or the ribs, and the shot let go as a short cone that moves him. It is placed, never swung, and never at the face

_reuse: how strongly a shape that is already posed, or one swap or re-aim from it, is preferred. A re-aim Animation measured as ok is free; one at the edge needs a look, so it is preferred less. These are the first slice's values: lower them toward 1 and identity decides more, at the cost of new key sets
_rejected: shapes a review turned down, by fighter: never proposed again
